subject: High error spikes & token timeouts on dedicated pool — evidence request / SLA bridge
messages:
From: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@nebula.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-team@nebula.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Sep 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High error spikes & token timeouts on prod-dedicated pool

Hi Karthik —

We started seeing repeated 5xx spikes and token timeouts from our dedicated pool (pool-id: nb-dedicated-west-1) starting ~08:45 PDT. Impact is intermittent but affects roughly 12% of requests across three services (text-generation, chat-stream). Attached a small sample of service logs (service-logs-sample.txt).

Sample request ids: r-7b3f1a2, r-7b3f1a9, r-7b3f2c0. Latency jumps to 6–12s and some calls return 502/504. Can you confirm receipt and tell us what evidence you need from our side? We’re on a signed Dedicated contract and need an SLA bridging plan while you investigate.

Elena
Elena Moreno
Head of Platform Ops — Nebula AI
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@nebula.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Sep 2029 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error spikes & token timeouts on prod-dedicated pool

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the heads up and for the logs. I’ve looped in Ben (engineering liaison for Dedicated) and Monica (Customer Ops) so we can move quickly. We’re treating this as a high-priority incident.

What we need from you right now to accelerate triage:
- A short list of 3 representative request IDs (you already included some — thanks).
- Any recent configuration changes on your side (scaling policies, connection pools) in the last 24 hours.
- If possible, a short window of packet captures for one affected instance (optional).

Ben/Monica — can you validate whether this looks like a capacity/backpressure issue vs. a network proxy failure? Monica, please start an ops bridge with the Nebula on our side and prepare a provisional SLA credit offer.

We’ll follow up with a preliminary timeline for containment within the next 2 hours.

Regards,
Karthik
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@nebula.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Sep 2029 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error spikes & token timeouts on prod-dedicated pool

Thanks, Karthik. Elena — quick note from Eng Ops: we’re seeing transient queue pileups on the allocator for that tenant group coincident with increased preemption activity. Preliminary hypothesis: aggressive preemption + cold KV cache and request-level tail latency.

I’m attaching a small helper script you can run on one representative host to capture GPU metrics and process stacks for 5m (capture_gpu_metrics.sh). If you can run that and send the output back, it will help us correlate. Please run as sudo and send the .tar.gz produced.

We’re spinning up a temporary throttle rule to reduce preemption aggressiveness and will monitor for the next hour. If the issue drops out, we’ll follow with a rolling configuration change.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Site Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachment: capture_gpu_metrics.sh (script stub)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@nebula.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Sep 2029 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error spikes & token timeouts on prod-dedicated pool

Elena —

Thanks for running the capture and sending back the archive. Our initial analysis (attached diagnostic_summary.txt) shows these findings:
- Root cause (preliminary): allocator’s preemption threshold incorrectly applied to your reserved slice during a background rebalancing window; this caused multiple GPU worker evictions and cold starts.
- Observable impact: sudden KV cache misses, increased tokenization latencies and a spike in in-flight queue length.
- Time window: ~08:42–09:10 PDT.

Immediate actions taken:
- Rolled back the aggressive preemption rule at 10:15 PDT.
- Applied a temporary retry / backoff tuning for your tenant route to reduce visible 5xxs.
- Increased warm standbys for your pool for the next 24h.

Next steps we’re committing to:
1) Full postmortem with timelines and RCA by EOD tomorrow.
2) A targeted config change to prevent preemption of reserved slices during rebalancing.
3) A one-time SLA bridging credit proposal (draft attached: sla_comp_offer_v1.pdf).

Attachments: diagnostic_summary.txt, redwood_debug_dump_2029-09-02.tar.gz

We’ll schedule a 30-minute debrief with your ops team first thing tomorrow to walk through the timeline and validation plan.

-Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Reliability Lead — Redwood Inference
From: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@nebula.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Sep 2029 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High error spikes & token timeouts on prod-dedicated pool

Team —

Appreciate the quick analysis and the temporary mitigations. A couple of asks before the debrief:
- Can you include explicit timestamps (UTC and local) for every event in the postmortem? We need them for our compliance logs.
- Please provide the list of evicted worker node IDs and the exact preemption rule change you rolled back.
- We’ll accept the proposed SLA bridging credit in principle — send us the formal DocuSign link and the exact credit amount calculation.

I’ve attached an additional log sample where we saw a 502 at 08:49:16 PDT (service-logs-sample.txt). Looking forward to the debrief.

Thanks,
Elena
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Elena —

Confirmed. We’ll include full UTC/local timestamps in the postmortem and enumerate evicted node IDs and the preemption rule change. Monica will circulate the formal credit calculation and a DocuSign link for approval shortly.

Planned schedule: 30-min joint debrief at Tue 03 Sep 2029 13:00 PDT (we created a calendar invite and a short ops runbook in the shared Drive — link attached). Please let me know if that time works or if you prefer 14:00.

- Monica: prepare SLA credit calculation + DocuSign (ETA: 3 hours).

Thanks again for the partnership here — we’ll aim to make the postmortem as actionable as possible.

Best,
